risk_reasons: The change controls durable Send batch parent terminalization and its exactly-once close receipt.
goal: A Settled batch closes its Send batch parent for every valid UUID casing accepted at an input boundary.
non_goals: Remove boundary canonicalization already present in approveBatch and haltBatch.
Implement the #630 releaser or send worker.
user_visible_behavior: A mixed-case batch id cannot strand an otherwise Settled batch with a running Send batch parent.
invariants: closeBatchIfSettled remains the single owner of batch closure.
The Send batch parent and close step terminalize exactly once behind the winning batch CAS.
Canonical lowercase callers retain identical behavior.
Malformed UUIDs retain the existing database rejection behavior.
edge_cases: Uppercase and mixed-case UUIDs resolve the same batch and Send batch parent as lowercase UUIDs.
A second close attempt writes no duplicate close step.
Existing HTTP callers remain protected by their entry-point canonicalization.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/lib/solicitation/approval.ts canonicalizes request-supplied batch ids once at each verb entry point.
src/lib/solicitation/outreach.ts owns Settled batch closure and parent terminalization.
src/lib/solicitation/__tests__/outreach-close.integration.test.ts verifies closure through the public transaction seam.
test_seams: closeBatchIfSettled invoked in a live database transaction with a mixed-case batch id.
tests_to_add: closes the Send batch parent when the batch id uses mixed case
rollback_plan: Revert the single callee-local canonicalization and its regression test; no schema, data repair, flag change, or remote operation is involved.
observability: The existing Send batch close step and parent terminal state remain the durable success signals.
